newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--More buying should NAPM be weak.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--More buying should NAPM be weak.

text.p: Another wave of key economic statistics is expected to keep the U.S. Treasury market busy on Thursday, with players figuring the data could mostly help rather than hurt what has become a surging market.
The highlight of the day looks to be the National Association of Purchasing Management's manufacturing index for April -- due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
The fear in the market -- even though it is hard to tell given the impressive two-day rally -- is the NAPM will follow the Chicago version and come in robust.
Yet, should the report come in as expected or even weaker, the market will most likely add to its recent gains, analysts agreed.
NAPM's overall index is expected to have declined to 53.6 in April, from 55.0 in March, according to a Reuters poll.

"People are now thinking that the (Federal Reserve) is off the hook (for a rate hike in May)," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market strategist at UBS Securities LLC. "So, as long as we don't get overheated statistics the market can grind higher purely on technicals."
"It will take some threatening economic data to reverse this technical bid in the marketplace."

Dimick said the rally, although triggered largely by bond- bullish data, has been mostly technical in nature, as those players who were short were forced to cover, while those "siting on cash" had to come off the sidelines and buy or face falling behind their benchmark indexes.
Indeed, for the better part of a week and a half before Tuesday, the market, for the most part, stuck to narrow ranges in the absence of significant economic data.

But after a lower than expected 0.6 percent rise in the first-quarter employment cost index on Tuesday and what was seen as an unsustainable 5.6 percent jump in first quarter growth, the market late Wednesday finds itself down about 25 basis points in yield across the curve.
The 30-year bond was at 95-28/32, up 12/32 from Tuesday, while its yield stands at 6.95 percent. Meanwhile, the two-year note was up 3/32 at 100-6/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
Market participants said the latest rally "squeezed" out much of the speculative shorts, which only has added to a favorable technical environment.
Also on Thursday, weekly jobless claims data are scheduled for release at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Claims in the week ended April 26 are seen flat at around 325,000.
Auto sales data are slated to be released throughout the day.

Economic data aside, the ongoing budget talks are also garnering plenty of attention, as Republicans and Democrats seek a compromise. News of progress in the talks contributed to the market's rally on Wednesday.
Dimick, though, warns that should talks collapse, it could turn into a classic case of "buy the rumor, sell the fact."
